# Results — Study 649 (Gold Seasonality): is September really gold's best month?

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Monthly log returns of **GLD**
(SPDR Gold Shares, the tradable, physically backed gold ETF) built from daily adjusted closes
resampled to month-end, plus the **^IRX** 13-week T-bill yield used only to build an
excess-of-cash return for the timer/buy-and-hold race. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprints `44f6ff1685e4` (GLD) /
`03b833c2e7e3` (^IRX).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted GLD closes (5,436 rows) + ^IRX 13-week T-bill yield (5,431 rows), 2004-11-18 → 2026-06-30 (GLD's own inception), resampled to **259 month-end log returns** |
| Calendar under test | the folklore's own claim, hardcoded: **strong = September** (Indian wedding-season + pre-Diwali physical demand, year-end restocking); **weak/lull = May–Aug** (the quiet Northern-hemisphere summer) — facts, not fitted, see `STRONG_MONTHS` / `SUMMER_MONTHS` in [`gold_seasonality/data.py`](../gold_seasonality/data.py) |
| Statistics | one-sample naive + **Newey-West (HAC)** *t* per calendar month (12 cells) with a **Bonferroni** bar for 12 simultaneous tests; Welch *t* for September-vs-rest and summer-vs-rest; a circular block-bootstrap CI (5,000 draws, 12-month blocks) on the September spread; Wilson interval on the timer's hit rate |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: the "own gold only in September" timer sets its position from the fixed calendar alone — September is the same slot every year, so no signal-to-trade lag is needed (the monthly return already runs August-close → September-close). Round-trip costs: 2 one-way legs/yr × 5/10 bps × NAV, charged only on the active month |
| Era split | **2013-04-01**, justified: the 2013-04-12/15 gold crash (spot −13% in two sessions, the worst two-day drop in ~30 years) — the documented end of the 2001–2012 bull "supercycle" and the start of the decade-long range-bound regime |

No survivorship on the Signal axis: GLD is a single, continuously-listed physically-backed ETF
(no basket, no roll, no dividend adjustment needed), not a cross-sectional panel.

## The headline — 12-cell month-of-year table, Bonferroni-corrected

Bonferroni bar for 12 simultaneous tests (α = 0.05/12, df=257): **|t| ≥ 2.89**.

| Month | Mean | n | naive *t* | HAC *t* | |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| Jan | **+3.47%** | 22 | +3.22 | **+3.77** | **survives Bonferroni** |
| Feb | +1.21% | 22 | +1.19 | +1.52 | |
| Mar | −0.08% | 22 | −0.08 | −0.08 | |
| Apr | +1.57% | 22 | +1.66 | +1.98 | |
| May | −0.54% | 22 | −0.63 | −0.55 | |
| Jun | −0.85% | 22 | −0.72 | −0.99 | |
| Jul | +1.15% | 21 | +1.23 | +1.65 | |
| Aug | +1.47% | 21 | +1.49 | +1.35 | |
| **Sep** | **+0.03%** | 21 | +0.02 | +0.02 | the claim under test |
| Oct | +0.64% | 21 | +0.56 | +0.74 | |
| Nov | +0.94% | 21 | +0.75 | +0.62 | |
| Dec | +0.71% | 22 | +0.72 | +0.65 | |

**Cells clearing the Bonferroni bar: 1/12 — and it isn't September.** The only calendar month
whose one-sample HAC *t* survives 12-way multiple testing is **January** (+3.47%/mo, HAC
*t* = +3.77) — a genuinely large, statistically hard-to-dismiss month-of-year effect, but a
*different* claim (a gold "January effect"), not the one under test, and not investigated further
here. September itself is dead flat: **+0.03%** average, essentially a rounding error, with
naive and HAC *t*'s of **+0.02**.

## September vs the rest — the headline claim

| quantity | September | other 11 months |
|---|--:|--:|
| mean monthly return | **+0.03%** | +0.88% |
| n | 21 | 238 |
| spread | **−0.85%** | |
| Welch *t* | **−0.64** | |

September doesn't just fail to clear the bar — the point estimate has the **wrong sign**: the
average September is *below* the average non-September month. **Circular block-bootstrap 95% CI**
on the spread (5,000 draws, 12-month blocks, respecting the annual seasonal structure):
**[−3.23%, +1.60%]** — comfortably straddling zero, more than three times wider than the point
estimate itself.

## Summer (May–Aug) vs the rest — the "lull" half of the claim

| quantity | summer (May–Aug) | other 8 months |
|---|--:|--:|
| mean monthly return | +0.29% | +1.07% |
| n | 86 | 173 |
| spread | **−0.79%** | |
| Welch *t* | **−1.24** | |

Directionally consistent with a lull (summer underperforms), but **not significant** — and summer
itself is still *positive on average* (+0.29%/mo), not the flat-to-negative "quiet season" the
folklore implies. Not a certified effect either way.

## Era contrast — September, pre vs post the 2013 gold crash

Split at **2013-04-01** (the 2013-04-12/15 gold crash — an externally-dated, justified break, not
snooped).

| era | September mean | n | within-era Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2004 → 2013-04 | +2.49% | 8 | +0.53 |
| 2013-04 → 2026 | −1.48% | 13 | −1.60 |
| Welch *t* of the difference (late − early) | | | **−1.40** |

If anything, September's point estimate has gone from mildly positive to mildly negative since
the 2013 crash — but **neither era is individually significant**, and the difference itself is
**not certified** (*t* = −1.40). There is no honest reading here where September was once real
and has since decayed: it was never significant in either era.

## Third axis — "own gold only in September" timer vs buy-and-hold

Long GLD only in September (calendar-known rule, zero look-ahead), cash (^IRX) the other 11
months; 2 one-way legs/yr × cost × NAV, charged only on the active month. Both sides raced
excess-of-cash so a partly-invested timer isn't flattered for merely holding less risk.

| | Sharpe (excess of cash) | CAGR | Vol (ann.) | Max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Buy & hold** | **+0.47** | **+8.59%/yr** | 17.1% | −46.7% |
| Timer, gross | −0.02 | +1.48%/yr | 5.8% | −28.6% |
| Timer, net (5 bps) | −0.04 | +1.38%/yr | | |
| Timer, net (10 bps) | −0.05 | +1.28%/yr | | |

| | value |
|---|--:|
| September hit rate | **9/21 = 42.9%** (Wilson 95% [24.5%, 63.5%]) |

Owning gold only in September doesn't merely fail to beat buy-and-hold — it **gives up almost
the entire return**: +1.3–1.5%/yr vs +8.6%/yr, with a negative excess-of-cash Sharpe against
buy-and-hold's +0.47, and a hit rate (43%) that is nominally *below* a coin flip. Sitting in cash
11 months a year on an asset that spent 21+ years compounding at ~8.6%/yr forgoes almost all of
gold's return, for nothing in exchange.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic i.i.d. monthly-return world with a TUNABLE planted September-premium /
summer-discount pair; no network.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (seasonal = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.31** (sd 1.08), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/20 seeds** |
| planted seasonal = +3.0%/mo (seed 649) | **+6.58** |

The detector fires at roughly the nominal false-positive rate on the null (2/20, in line with
α ≈ 0.05 given sampling noise across seeds) and lights up decisively on a planted calendar.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** September's monthly return is **+0.03%** — a rounding error — against
  +0.88% for the other 11 months (**wrong sign**, Welch *t* = **−0.64**), with a bootstrap CI
  **[−3.23%, +1.60%]** that straddles zero. Zero of 12 calendar months survive the Bonferroni
  bar *in September's favor*; the one month that does survive (January, HAC *t* = +3.77) is a
  different, untested claim. The summer "lull" is directionally present but not significant
  (*t* = −1.24), and the pre/post-2013 contrast shows no era where September was ever
  certified. There is no real September seasonal on the real GLD tape.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even setting Signal aside, the "own gold only in September" timer
  gives up nearly all of gold's return (+1.3–1.5%/yr net vs +8.6%/yr buy-and-hold), posts a
  **negative** excess-of-cash Sharpe (−0.02 to −0.05 vs buy-and-hold's +0.47), and its hit rate
  (42.9%, Wilson [24.5%, 63.5%]) is nominally below a coin flip.
- **"Gold's 'best month'?" — BUSTED.** September is not statistically distinguishable from an
  average month, is not the sample's actual best month (January is, on a different claim
  entirely), and a strategy built to harvest it loses to simply buying and holding gold.
